units.title: Primi passi
units.intro: Everyday words, the 8 verbs you will use most, and phrases Italians say every day.

words.ex: È una persona molto gentile.
words.exEn: They're a very kind person.

words.ex: Quell'uomo è mio zio.
words.exEn: That man is my uncle.

words.ex: La donna al bar è di Napoli.
words.exEn: The woman at the bar is from Naples.

words.ex: Il bambino dorme ancora.
words.exEn: The child is still sleeping.

words.ex: Stasera esco con un amico.
words.exEn: Tonight I'm going out with a friend.

words.ex: La mia famiglia vive a Roma.
words.exEn: My family lives in Rome.

words.ex: Mia madre lavora in ospedale.
words.exEn: My mother works at a hospital.

words.ex: Mio padre cucina molto bene.
words.exEn: My father cooks very well.

words.ex: Ho un fratello più grande.
words.exEn: I have an older brother.

words.ex: Mia sorella studia medicina.
words.exEn: My sister studies medicine.

words.ex: Il figlio di Marco ha dieci anni.
words.exEn: Marco's son is ten.

words.ex: La figlia di Anna vive a Londra.
words.exEn: Anna's daughter lives in London.

words.ex: Il marito di Anna è medico.
words.exEn: Anna's husband is a doctor.

words.ex: Mia moglie parla tre lingue.
words.exEn: My wife speaks three languages.

words.ex: Il ragazzo di Sara è simpatico.
words.exEn: Sara's boyfriend is nice.

words.ex: Quella ragazza è mia cugina.
words.exEn: That girl is my cousin.

words.ex: C'è tanta gente in piazza.
words.exEn: There are lots of people in the square.
words.note: Always singular: la gente è, never “sono”.

words.ex: Torno a casa alle sei.
words.exEn: I get home at six.

words.ex: La camera è piccola ma bella.
words.exEn: The bedroom is small but nice.

words.ex: Mangiamo in cucina.
words.exEn: We eat in the kitchen.

words.ex: Scusi, dov'è il bagno?
words.exEn: Excuse me, where's the bathroom?

words.ex: Chiudi la porta, per favore.
words.exEn: Close the door, please.

words.ex: Apro la finestra, fa caldo.
words.exEn: I'll open the window, it's hot.

words.ex: Stasera vado a letto presto.
words.exEn: Tonight I'm going to bed early.

words.ex: Un tavolo per due, per favore.
words.exEn: A table for two, please.

words.ex: Questa sedia è libera?
words.exEn: Is this chair free?

words.ex: Non trovo le chiavi.
words.exEn: I can't find the keys.

words.ex: Il mio telefono è scarico.
words.exEn: My phone is dead.

words.ex: Bologna è una città bellissima.
words.exEn: Bologna is a beautiful city.
words.note: Ends in an accent, so the plural doesn't change.

words.ex: Attento quando attraversi la strada.
words.exEn: Be careful when you cross the street.

words.ex: Prendo un caffè al bar.
words.exEn: I'll have a coffee at the bar.

words.ex: Acqua frizzante o naturale?
words.exEn: Sparkling or still water?

words.ex: Il pane è ancora caldo.
words.exEn: The bread is still warm.

words.ex: Un bicchiere di vino rosso, grazie.
words.exEn: A glass of red wine, thanks.

words.ex: Mi piace il formaggio.
words.exEn: I like cheese.

words.ex: Non mangio carne.
words.exEn: I don't eat meat.

words.ex: Il pesce qui è freschissimo.
words.exEn: The fish here is really fresh.

words.ex: Mangio frutta ogni giorno.
words.exEn: I eat fruit every day.
words.note: Uncountable, like “fruit” in English.

words.ex: Faccio colazione alle otto.
words.exEn: I have breakfast at eight.

words.ex: Il pranzo è pronto!
words.exEn: Lunch is ready!

words.ex: Vieni a cena da noi?
words.exEn: Are you coming to dinner at our place?

words.ex: Il conto, per favore.
words.exEn: The bill, please.

words.ex: Che giorno è oggi?
words.exEn: What day is it today?

words.ex: Buona notte, a domani!
words.exEn: Good night, see you tomorrow!

words.ex: La mattina bevo un caffè.
words.exEn: In the morning I drink a coffee.

words.ex: Di sera esco con gli amici.
words.exEn: In the evening I go out with friends.

words.ex: Lavoro cinque giorni a settimana.
words.exEn: I work five days a week.

words.ex: Il mese prossimo vado in Sicilia.
words.exEn: Next month I'm going to Sicily.

words.ex: Ho trent'anni.
words.exEn: I'm thirty years old.
words.note: Age uses avere: ho trent'anni.

words.ex: Che ore sono?
words.exEn: What time is it?

words.ex: Oggi fa bel tempo.
words.exEn: The weather is nice today.

words.ex: A domani!
words.exEn: See you tomorrow!

words.ex: Ieri sono rimasto a casa.
words.exEn: Yesterday I stayed home.

words.ex: Adesso non posso, scusa.
words.exEn: I can't right now, sorry.

words.ex: Marco arriva sempre in ritardo.
words.exEn: Marco is always late.

words.ex: Non bevo mai il latte.
words.exEn: I never drink milk.
words.note: Pairs with non: non… mai.

words.ex: Questa pizza è buonissima!
words.exEn: This pizza is delicious!

words.ex: Che bella giornata!
words.exEn: What a beautiful day!

words.ex: La casa è grande.
words.exEn: The house is big.

words.ex: Ho una macchina piccola.
words.exEn: I have a small car.

words.ex: È il mio nuovo lavoro.
words.exEn: It's my new job.

words.ex: Questo palazzo è molto vecchio.
words.exEn: This building is very old.

words.ex: Oggi fa molto caldo.
words.exEn: It's very hot today.

words.ex: L'acqua è fredda.
words.exEn: The water is cold.

words.ex: Questo esercizio è facile.
words.exEn: This exercise is easy.

words.ex: È difficile trovare parcheggio.
words.exEn: It's hard to find parking.

words.ex: Sono stanco morto.
words.exEn: I'm dead tired.

words.ex: Sono contento di vederti.
words.exEn: I'm glad to see you.

words.ex: Vengo anch'io!
words.exEn: I'm coming too!

words.ex: Mi piace molto.
words.exEn: I like it a lot.

words.ex: Dormo poco.
words.exEn: I don't sleep much.

words.ex: Sei ancora a casa?
words.exEn: Are you still at home?

words.ex: Hai già mangiato?
words.exEn: Have you already eaten?

words.ex: Abito qui vicino.
words.exEn: I live near here.

words.ex: Metti la borsa lì.
words.exEn: Put the bag there.

words.ex: Perché ridi?
words.exEn: Why are you laughing?

words.ex: Quando parti?
words.exEn: When are you leaving?

words.ex: Dove abiti?
words.exEn: Where do you live?

words.ex: Come ti chiami?
words.exEn: What's your name?

verbs.note: Also the helper verb for movement and change: sono andato, è arrivata. With essere, the past participle agrees with the subject (-o/-a/-i/-e).
ex: Sono di Milano, ma vivo a Torino.
I'm from Milan, but I live in Turin.

verbs.note: Italians have age, hunger and feelings: avere fame (be hungry), sete (thirsty), freddo (cold), sonno (sleepy), ragione (be right).
ex: Are you hungry? Let's go eat.

verbs.note: Used for weather and dozens of daily actions: fa freddo (it's cold), fare colazione (have breakfast), fare la spesa (do the shopping), fare una domanda (ask a question).
ex: What do you do for work?

verbs.note: andare a + city (vado a Roma), andare in + country or region (vado in Italia), andare da + person (vado da Marco).
ex: We're going to Italy in June.

verbs.note: Come stai? — Sto bene. Also stare + gerund for “right now”: sto mangiando (I'm eating).
ex: How are you? — I'm fine, thanks.
I'm working, I'll call you later.

verbs.note: Vorrei (I would like) is the polite way to order or ask. Followed directly by an infinitive: voglio dormire.
ex: Do you want to come with us?

verbs.note: Posso…? is how you ask permission. Potrebbe…? is a very polite request.
Your model for every regular -are verb (abitare, lavorare, mangiare…). parlare con someone, parlare di something.
ex: Let's talk about the film after dinner.

phrases.note: Formal: Come sta?
phrases.ex: Ciao Luca, come stai? — Bene, grazie, e tu?
phrases.exEn: Hi Luca, how are you? — Fine, thanks, and you?

phrases.ex: Sono Giulia. — Piacere, Marco.
phrases.exEn: I'm Giulia. — Nice to meet you, I'm Marco.

phrases.ex: Ci vediamo domani in ufficio.
phrases.exEn: See you tomorrow at the office.

phrases.lit: What of it do you think?
phrases.ex: Ho trovato un appartamento. Che ne pensi?
phrases.exEn: I found an apartment. What do you think?

phrases.ex: Vieni stasera? — Dipende da quando finisco.
phrases.exEn: Are you coming tonight? — Depends when I finish.

phrases.ex: Ho voglia di una pizza.
phrases.exEn: I feel like a pizza.

phrases.ex: Il treno è in orario. — Meno male!
phrases.exEn: The train is on time. — Thank goodness!

phrases.ex: Andiamo al mare? — Magari!
phrases.exEn: Shall we go to the beach? — I wish!

phrases.en: I can't manage it / I can't take it
phrases.ex: Sono troppo stanco, non ce la faccio più.
phrases.exEn: I'm too tired, I can't go on.

phrases.ex: Dov'è Marco? — Boh.
phrases.exEn: Where's Marco? — No idea.

phrases.ex: Dai, vieni con noi!
phrases.exEn: Come on, come with us!

phrases.ex: Allora, cosa prendiamo?
phrases.exEn: So, what are we having?

phrases.ex: È caro, però è buono.
phrases.exEn: It's expensive, but it's good.

phrases.ex: Comunque, parliamo d'altro.
phrases.exEn: Anyway, let's talk about something else.

units.title: Chi sono
units.intro: How to introduce yourself, say where you're from and what you do, give your details, and count from 0 to 100.

words.ex: Il mio nome è Sara.
words.exEn: My name is Sara.

words.ex: Qual è il tuo cognome?
words.exEn: What's your surname?
words.note: Forms ask for nome and cognome separately.

words.ex: Non dico mai la mia età.
words.exEn: I never tell anyone my age.
words.note: Ends in an accent, so the plural doesn't change.

words.ex: Mi dai il tuo indirizzo?
words.exEn: Can you give me your address?

words.ex: Abito in via Garibaldi, 12.
words.exEn: I live at 12 Via Garibaldi.
words.note: In addresses the number comes after the street name.

words.ex: Il mio cellulare è scarico.
words.exEn: My phone is dead.
words.note: Often shortened to il cell.

words.ex: Ti mando un'email stasera.
words.exEn: I'll send you an email tonight.
words.note: Feminine (un'email) and the plural doesn't change. Also written mail.

words.ex: Quando è il tuo compleanno?
words.exEn: When is your birthday?

words.ex: Il signor Rossi è il mio vicino.
words.exEn: Mr Rossi is my neighbour.
words.note: Drops the final -e before a name: signor Rossi.

words.ex: Buongiorno, signora Bianchi!
words.exEn: Good morning, Mrs Bianchi!

words.ex: Sei sposata o single?
words.exEn: Are you married or single?
words.note: sposato con someone: married to.

words.ex: Mio cugino è ancora single.
words.exEn: My cousin is still single.
words.note: Borrowed from English; it never changes form.

words.ex: Chi è quella ragazza?
words.exEn: Who's that girl?

words.ex: Qual è il tuo numero?
words.exEn: What's your number?
words.note: Before è it becomes qual è — no apostrophe!

words.ex: Ciao Marco, a dopo!
words.exEn: Bye Marco, see you later!
words.note: Informal, for both hello and goodbye.

words.ex: Buongiorno, posso entrare?
words.exEn: Good morning, may I come in?
words.note: Used until early afternoon; then switch to buonasera.

words.ex: Buonasera a tutti!
words.exEn: Good evening, everyone!

words.ex: Grazie, arrivederci!
words.exEn: Thank you, goodbye!
words.note: Very formal version: arrivederLa.

words.ex: Grazie mille per l'aiuto!
words.exEn: Thanks so much for your help!

words.ex: Grazie! — Prego, figurati.
words.exEn: Thanks! — You're welcome, don't mention it.
words.note: Also said when inviting someone in or to go first.

words.ex: L'Italia è un paese bellissimo.
words.exEn: Italy is a beautiful country.

words.ex: Ho amici in tutto il mondo.
words.exEn: I have friends all over the world.

words.ex: Mia sorella lavora all'estero.
words.exEn: My sister works abroad.
words.note: Always with the article: all'estero (abroad), dall'estero (from abroad).

words.ex: Quante lingue parli?
words.exEn: How many languages do you speak?

words.ex: Di che nazionalità sei?
words.exEn: What nationality are you?

words.ex: Ci sono molti studenti stranieri qui.
words.exEn: There are lots of foreign students here.

words.ex: Vivo in Italia da due anni.
words.exEn: I've been living in Italy for two years.
words.note: Countries take the article: l'Italia è bella, but in Italia.

words.ex: Lei viene dagli Stati Uniti.
words.exEn: She comes from the United States.
words.note: Plural: negli Stati Uniti (in the US).

words.ex: Studio inglese in Inghilterra.
words.exEn: I'm studying English in England.
words.note: For the UK: il Regno Unito.

words.ex: La Francia è vicina.
words.exEn: France is close by.

words.ex: Mio padre lavora in Germania.
words.exEn: My father works in Germany.

words.ex: Andiamo in Spagna a luglio.
words.exEn: We're going to Spain in July.

words.ex: Parli italiano molto bene!
words.exEn: You speak Italian very well!
words.note: Nationalities and languages are written with a small letter.

words.ex: Il mio capo è inglese.
words.exEn: My boss is English.
words.note: Ends in -e: same form for men and women (un ragazzo inglese, una ragazza inglese).

words.ex: Ho un'amica americana.
words.exEn: I have an American friend.

words.ex: Il francese è difficile per me.
words.exEn: French is hard for me.

words.ex: I miei colleghi sono tedeschi.
words.exEn: My colleagues are German.
words.note: Plural: tedeschi, tedesche.

words.ex: Parlo un po' di spagnolo.
words.exEn: I speak a bit of Spanish.

words.ex: Studio cinese all'università.
words.exEn: I study Chinese at university.

words.ex: È una città molto europea.
words.exEn: It's a very European city.

words.ex: Cerco lavoro a Milano.
words.exEn: I'm looking for work in Milan.

words.ex: Fa il mestiere di suo padre.
words.exEn: He does the same job as his father.

words.ex: Lavoro in un'azienda di moda.
words.exEn: I work for a fashion company.

words.ex: Sono uno studente di medicina.
words.exEn: I'm a medical student.
words.note: Feminine: la studentessa.

words.ex: Mia zia è insegnante di musica.
words.exEn: My aunt is a music teacher.
words.note: Same form for a man or a woman: l'insegnante, un'insegnante.

words.ex: Il mio medico è molto bravo.
words.exEn: My doctor is very good.
words.note: Plural medici (soft c). Also il dottore / la dottoressa.

words.ex: Fa l'infermiere in ospedale.
words.exEn: He's a nurse at the hospital.
words.note: Feminine: l'infermiera.

words.ex: Lei è avvocato a Firenze.
words.exEn: She's a lawyer in Florence.

words.ex: Voglio diventare ingegnere.
words.exEn: I want to become an engineer.
words.note: Ingegnere is also used as a title: l'ingegner Verdi.

words.ex: Mio fratello fa l'architetto.
words.exEn: My brother is an architect.

words.ex: Sono impiegata in banca.
words.exEn: I'm a clerk at a bank.

words.ex: Il commesso è molto gentile.
words.exEn: The shop assistant is very kind.

words.ex: Lavora come operaio in fabbrica.
words.exEn: He works as a factory worker.

words.ex: Mia madre è una cuoca bravissima.
words.exEn: My mother is a brilliant cook.

words.ex: La giornalista fa molte domande.
words.exEn: The journalist asks lots of questions.
words.note: Ends in -a but can be masculine: il giornalista / la giornalista; plural i giornalisti / le giornaliste.

words.ex: Il poliziotto mi aiuta subito.
words.exEn: The police officer helps me straight away.

words.ex: Domani vado dal parrucchiere.
words.exEn: Tomorrow I'm going to the hairdresser's.

words.ex: Faccio il programmatore da casa.
words.exEn: I work from home as a programmer.
words.note: Feminine: la programmatrice.

words.ex: Mio nonno è pensionato.
words.exEn: My grandfather is retired.
words.note: Also sono in pensione: I'm retired.

words.ex: Adesso sono disoccupato, purtroppo.
words.exEn: I'm unemployed at the moment, unfortunately.

words.ex: Il prefisso comincia con zero.
words.exEn: The area code starts with zero.

words.ex: Ho solo un fratello.
words.exEn: I only have one brother.
words.note: Before a noun it works like the article: un libro, una casa.

words.ex: Abbiamo due figli.
words.exEn: We have two children.

words.ex: Abito al numero tre.
words.exEn: I live at number three.
words.note: No accent alone, but ventitré, trentatré take one.

words.ex: Siamo in quattro stasera.
words.exEn: There are four of us tonight.

words.ex: Lavoro cinque giorni a settimana.
words.exEn: I work five days a week.

words.ex: Mia figlia ha sei anni.
words.exEn: My daughter is six.

words.ex: Il corso dura sette mesi.
words.exEn: The course lasts seven months.

words.ex: Ho otto colleghi.
words.exEn: I have eight colleagues.

words.ex: Il codice è nove, due, uno.
words.exEn: The code is nine, two, one.

words.ex: Parlo italiano da dieci anni.
words.exEn: I've been speaking Italian for ten years.

words.ex: Siamo in undici, come una squadra.
words.exEn: There are eleven of us, like a team.

words.ex: La mia classe ha dodici studenti.
words.exEn: My class has twelve students.

words.ex: Ho sedici anni.
words.exEn: I'm sixteen.
words.note: 11–16 end in -dici; from 17 it flips: diciassette, diciotto, diciannove.

words.ex: Il diciassette è un numero sfortunato.
words.exEn: Seventeen is an unlucky number.
words.note: In Italy 17 is the unlucky number, not 13.

words.ex: L'autobus passa ogni venti minuti.
words.exEn: The bus comes every twenty minutes.

words.ex: Mio figlio ha ventun anni.
words.exEn: My son is twenty-one.
words.note: Tens drop their final vowel before uno and otto: ventuno, ventotto, trentuno.

words.ex: Il biglietto costa trenta euro.
words.exEn: The ticket costs thirty euros.

words.ex: Mia madre ha cinquant'anni.
words.exEn: My mother is fifty.
words.note: Then sessanta, settanta, ottanta, novanta.

words.ex: Ci sono cento persone alla festa.
words.exEn: There are a hundred people at the party.
words.note: Never uno cento: just cento.

verbs.en: to be called; to be named
verbs.note: Italians don't say “my name is” but “I call myself”: mi chiamo Anna. Without si, chiamare means to call (someone).
ex: Mi chiamo Luca, e tu come ti chiami?
My name's Luca, and what's yours?

verbs.note: abitare a + city, abitare in + country or street (abito in via Roma). Stress falls on the first syllable: àbito.
ex: Abito a Bologna con due amici.
I live in Bologna with two friends.

verbs.note: lavorare in + place or field (in banca, in ufficio), lavorare come + job, lavorare per + company.
ex: I work as a nurse at the hospital.

verbs.note: The i of the stem isn't doubled: tu studi, not studii. Studiare is also “to go to school/university”: studio a Padova.
ex: I've been studying Italian for six months.
Mia sorella studia legge a Roma.
My sister studies law in Rome.

verbs.note: venire da = to come from: vengo da Londra. Vieni con noi? — are you coming with us?
ex: Are you coming to the party on Saturday?

verbs.note: dire a qualcuno: to tell someone. Come si dice…? = how do you say…? Don't confuse with parlare (to speak).
ex: What are you saying? I can't hear you.
Mi ha detto il suo nome.

verbs.en: to know (a fact); to know how to
verbs.note: sapere = know facts or skills (so nuotare); conoscere = know people and places. Non lo so = I don't know.
ex: Do you know where the station is?

verbs.en: to know (people, places); to meet (for the first time)
verbs.note: In the past it means “to meet”: ho conosciuto Paolo a Roma = I met Paolo in Rome. Mind the sound: conosco (hard), conosci (soft).
ex: Do you know a good restaurant around here?

phrases.ex: Come ti chiami? — Mi chiamo Elena.
phrases.exEn: What's your name? — I'm Elena.

phrases.note: Also means “What's his/her name?” — context decides.
phrases.ex: Scusi, come si chiama? — Mario Bianchi.
phrases.exEn: Excuse me, what's your name? — Mario Bianchi.

phrases.note: Formal: Le presento…
phrases.ex: Ti presento mia sorella, Giulia. — Ciao!
phrases.exEn: This is my sister, Giulia. — Hi!

phrases.note: Men say lieto, women lieta.
phrases.ex: Le presento il dottor Neri. — Molto lieta.
phrases.exEn: May I introduce Dr Neri. — Pleased to meet you.

phrases.note: Formal: Di dov'è? Answer with Sono di + city.
phrases.ex: Di dove sei? — Sono di Palermo.
phrases.exEn: Where are you from? — I'm from Palermo.

phrases.lit: How many years do you have?
phrases.ex: Quanti anni hai? — Ne ho ventotto.
phrases.exEn: How old are you? — I'm twenty-eight.

phrases.en: What do you do (for a living)?
phrases.note: Answer with faccio il/la + job: faccio la commessa.
phrases.ex: Che lavoro fai? — Faccio l'insegnante.
phrases.exEn: What do you do? — I'm a teacher.

phrases.lit: Can we give each other the tu?
phrases.note: dare del tu (informal) vs dare del Lei (formal).
phrases.ex: Possiamo darci del tu? — Certo, volentieri!
phrases.exEn: Shall we drop the formalities? — Of course, gladly!

phrases.ex: Mi chiamo Ghezzi. — Come si scrive?
phrases.exEn: My name is Ghezzi. — How do you spell it?

phrases.ex: Come si dice “nurse” in italiano? — Infermiere.
phrases.exEn: How do you say “nurse” in Italian? — Infermiere.

units.title: Al bar
units.intro: Everything you need to order drinks and food at an Italian bar or restaurant, talk about tastes and pay the bill.

words.ex: Un espresso al banco, per favore.
words.exEn: An espresso at the counter, please.
words.note: At the bar, just ask for un caffè — it means an espresso.

words.ex: Prendo un cappuccino e un cornetto.
words.exEn: I'll have a cappuccino and a croissant.
words.note: Italians drink it in the morning, rarely after a meal.

words.en: espresso with a dash of milk
words.ex: Per me un macchiato caldo.
words.exEn: A macchiato with hot milk for me.
words.note: latte macchiato is the opposite: a glass of milk with a little coffee.

words.ex: Vorrei un bicchiere di latte freddo.
words.exEn: I'd like a glass of cold milk.
words.note: False friend: ask for “un latte” and you'll get plain milk!

words.ex: Un tè al limone, grazie.
words.exEn: A lemon tea, thanks.

words.ex: D'inverno bevo la cioccolata calda.
words.exEn: In winter I drink hot chocolate.

words.ex: Un succo di pesca per il bambino.
words.exEn: A peach juice for the little one.

words.ex: Una spremuta d'arancia, per favore.
words.exEn: A fresh orange juice, please.
words.note: spremuta is fresh; succo usually comes from a bottle.

words.ex: Due birre piccole, per favore.
words.exEn: Two small beers, please.

words.ex: Che bibite avete?
words.exEn: What soft drinks do you have?

words.ex: Facciamo un aperitivo alle sette?
words.exEn: Shall we have an aperitivo at seven?
words.note: A social ritual: drinks with snacks before dinner.

words.ex: Senza ghiaccio, grazie.
words.exEn: No ice, thanks.

words.ex: Prendi lo zucchero nel caffè?
words.exEn: Do you take sugar in your coffee?

words.ex: Un'acqua frizzante, per favore.
words.exEn: A sparkling water, please.

words.ex: Preferisci l'acqua naturale o frizzante?
words.exEn: Do you prefer still or sparkling water?

words.ex: Il cornetto alla crema è buonissimo.
words.exEn: The custard croissant is delicious.
words.note: In the north it's often called brioche.

words.ex: Prendo un panino al prosciutto.
words.exEn: I'll have a ham sandwich.
words.note: One sandwich is a panino — panini is the plural.

words.ex: Al bar mangio un tramezzino veloce.
words.exEn: I have a quick sandwich at the bar.

words.ex: Ordiniamo una pizza margherita?
words.exEn: Shall we order a margherita pizza?

words.ex: La pasta è troppo cotta.
words.exEn: The pasta is overcooked.
words.note: In a pastry shop, una pasta is a small cake.

words.ex: Gli spaghetti alle vongole sono ottimi qui.
words.exEn: The spaghetti with clams is excellent here.
words.note: Plural in Italian: gli spaghetti sono.

words.ex: Come antipasto prendiamo i salumi.
words.exEn: For a starter we'll have cold cuts.
words.note: False friend: it's the dish before the pasta, not against it.

words.ex: Di primo ho preso il risotto.
words.exEn: For my first course I had risotto.

words.ex: Per secondo vorrei la bistecca.
words.exEn: For my main course I'd like the steak.

words.ex: Come contorno, patate al forno.
words.exEn: Roast potatoes on the side.
words.note: Ordered separately from the secondo.

words.ex: Avete spazio per il dolce?
words.exEn: Do you have room for dessert?

words.ex: Un'insalata mista, per favore.
words.exEn: A mixed salad, please.

words.ex: Mangio tanta verdura.
words.exEn: I eat lots of vegetables.
words.note: Usually singular and uncountable, like frutta.

words.ex: Due hamburger con patatine.
words.exEn: Two burgers with fries.
words.note: patatine fritte = fries; a bag of patatine = crisps.

words.ex: Il pollo arrosto è il piatto del giorno.
words.exEn: Roast chicken is today's special.

words.ex: La bistecca è al sangue.
words.exEn: The steak is rare.

words.ex: Prosciutto e melone, che buono!
words.exEn: Ham and melon, how tasty!
words.note: crudo = cured (Parma-style), cotto = cooked ham.

words.ex: Per me due uova e il pane tostato.
words.exEn: Two eggs and toast for me.
words.note: Irregular plural, and it turns feminine: un uovo, le uova.

words.ex: Un gelato al pistacchio, per favore.
words.exEn: A pistachio ice cream, please.

words.ex: La torta della nonna è fantastica.
words.exEn: Granny's custard tart is fantastic.

words.ex: Ci vediamo al bar sotto casa.
words.exEn: Let's meet at the café downstairs.
words.note: An Italian bar is mainly a café, open from breakfast time.

words.ex: Conosci un ristorante tranquillo?
words.exEn: Do you know a quiet restaurant?

words.ex: Stasera andiamo in pizzeria.
words.exEn: Tonight we're going to a pizzeria.

words.ex: Questa trattoria ha piatti tipici.
words.exEn: This trattoria has traditional dishes.

words.ex: Il cameriere porta il menù.
words.exEn: The waiter brings the menu.
words.note: Feminine: la cameriera. To call them, just say Scusi!

words.ex: Il bar è pieno di clienti.
words.exEn: The café is full of customers.
words.note: Same form for men and women: il/la cliente.

words.ex: Possiamo vedere il menù?
words.exEn: Can we see the menu?

words.ex: Qual è la specialità della casa?
words.exEn: What's the house speciality?

words.ex: Le porzioni sono enormi qui.
words.exEn: The portions here are huge.

words.ex: C'è un posto libero fuori?
words.exEn: Is there a free seat outside?

words.ex: Bevo il caffè al bancone.
words.exEn: I drink my coffee at the counter.
words.note: Standing at the counter (al banco) is cheaper than sitting down.

words.ex: Ci sediamo a un tavolino fuori?
words.exEn: Shall we sit at a table outside?

words.ex: Si paga alla cassa.
words.exEn: You pay at the till.
words.note: In many bars you pay at the cassa first, then order with the receipt.

words.ex: Ecco lo scontrino, grazie.
words.exEn: Here's the receipt, thank you.

words.ex: Lasciamo una mancia al cameriere?
words.exEn: Shall we leave the waiter a tip?

words.ex: Il coperto costa due euro.
words.exEn: The cover charge is two euros.
words.note: A fixed charge per person for bread and table, common in restaurants.

words.ex: Il servizio è compreso?
words.exEn: Is service included?

words.ex: Sono tre euro e cinquanta.
words.exEn: That's three euros fifty.
words.note: Never changes in the plural: dieci euro.

words.ex: Posso pagare con la carta?
words.exEn: Can I pay by card?

words.ex: Pago in contanti.
words.exEn: I'll pay cash.
words.note: Always plural: in contanti.

words.ex: Il piatto è caldo, attenzione!
words.exEn: The plate is hot, careful!

words.ex: Mi porta un altro bicchiere?
words.exEn: Could you bring me another glass?
words.note: Drinking glass = bicchiere; the material is vetro.

words.ex: Una tazza di tè, per favore.
words.exEn: A cup of tea, please.

words.ex: La tazzina è bollente.
words.exEn: The coffee cup is boiling hot.

words.ex: Scusi, manca una forchetta.
words.exEn: Excuse me, we're missing a fork.

words.ex: Questo coltello non taglia.
words.exEn: This knife doesn't cut.

words.ex: La minestra si mangia col cucchiaio.
words.exEn: You eat soup with a spoon.

words.ex: Mi serve un cucchiaino per il gelato.
words.exEn: I need a teaspoon for the ice cream.

words.ex: Mi passi un tovagliolo?
words.exEn: Can you pass me a napkin?

words.ex: Manca un po' di sale.
words.exEn: It needs a little salt.

words.ex: Ho una fame da lupi!
words.exEn: I'm starving!
words.note: With avere: ho fame = I'm hungry.

words.ex: Fa caldo, ho sete.
words.exEn: It's hot, I'm thirsty.
words.note: ho sete = I'm thirsty.

words.ex: Questo gelato è buonissimo!
words.exEn: This ice cream is delicious!

words.ex: Che torta deliziosa!
words.exEn: What a lovely cake!

words.ex: La pasta è troppo salata.
words.exEn: The pasta is too salty.
words.note: Colloquially, un conto salato is a steep bill.

words.ex: Bevo il caffè amaro.
words.exEn: I drink my coffee without sugar.
words.note: caffè amaro = unsweetened. Un amaro is also a herbal after-dinner liqueur.

words.ex: Questo sugo è piccante?
words.exEn: Is this sauce spicy?

words.ex: Il pesce è fresco oggi?
words.exEn: Is the fish fresh today?
words.note: Plural: freschi, fresche.

words.ex: Non mangio il pesce crudo.
words.exEn: I don't eat raw fish.

words.ex: Vorrei qualcosa di leggero.
words.exEn: I'd like something light.

words.ex: La lasagna è un po' pesante.
words.exEn: Lasagne is a bit heavy.

words.ex: Avete piatti vegetariani?
words.exEn: Do you have vegetarian dishes?

words.ex: Basta così, sono pieno!
words.exEn: That's enough, I'm full!

words.ex: Un altro caffè, per favore.
words.exEn: Another coffee, please.

words.ex: Un panino senza maionese.
words.exEn: A sandwich without mayo.

verbs.note: The i only keeps the g soft, so it disappears before e/i: mangi, mangerò. Mangiare fuori = to eat out.
ex: I haven't eaten meat for years.

verbs.note: Built on the old form bevere: bevo, bevuto. Future and conditional have -rr-: berrò, berrei.
ex: What are you drinking? — A beer.
I've drunk too much coffee today.

verbs.en: to take; to have (food/drink); to catch (transport)
verbs.note: The everyday way to order: prendo un cappuccino = I'll have a cappuccino. Irregular participle: preso.
ex: What are you having? — I'll have a juice.

verbs.note: Stress on the first syllable in the present: òrdino, òrdinano. Waiters ask: Avete già ordinato?
ex: Ho ordinato una pizza a domicilio.
I ordered a pizza for delivery.

verbs.note: No “for” needed: pago il caffè = I pay for the coffee. An h keeps the g hard: paghi, pagherò.
ex: Have you already paid the bill?

verbs.note: Mostly used in the 3rd person: quanto costa? (one thing), quanto costano? (several). Takes essere, so the participle agrees: la pizza è costata poco.
ex: Le birre sono costate dieci euro.

verbs.note: Works backwards: the thing liked is the subject. Mi piace il gelato, mi piacciono gli spaghetti. Past: mi è piaciuta la pizza.
Adds -isc- in the present, except for noi and voi: preferisco, but preferiamo. Preferire A a B = to prefer A to B.
ex: Would you rather sit inside or outside?

phrases.note: The polite standard for ordering anything.
phrases.ex: Vorrei un cappuccino e una spremuta.
phrases.exEn: I'd like a cappuccino and a fresh orange juice.

phrases.ex: E per lei? — Per me un tramezzino.
phrases.exEn: And for you? — I'll have a sandwich.

phrases.it: Un tavolo per due, per favore
phrases.lit: A table for two, for favour
phrases.ex: Buonasera, un tavolo per due, per favore. — Prego, da questa parte.
phrases.exEn: Good evening, a table for two, please. — Of course, this way.

phrases.note: Informal: Cosa mi consigli?
phrases.ex: Cosa mi consiglia? — Il risotto è ottimo oggi.
phrases.exEn: What do you recommend? — The risotto is excellent today.

phrases.note: Reply: Grazie, altrettanto! (Thanks, you too!)
phrases.ex: Ecco i primi. Buon appetito! — Grazie!
phrases.exEn: Here are your first courses. Enjoy! — Thanks!

phrases.note: Also Salute!
phrases.ex: Alla nostra amicizia! — Cin cin!
phrases.exEn: To our friendship! — Cheers!

phrases.note: In Italy the waiter won't bring it until you ask.
phrases.ex: Scusi! Il conto, per favore. — Subito.
phrases.exEn: Excuse me! The bill, please. — Right away.

phrases.ex: Due caffè. Quant'è? — Due euro e quaranta.
phrases.exEn: Two coffees. How much is it? — Two euros forty.

phrases.ex: Offro io stavolta. — Grazie, sei gentilissimo!
phrases.exEn: It's on me this time. — Thanks, that's so kind of you!

phrases.lit: Let's do it the Roman way
phrases.note: Each person pays an equal share.
phrases.ex: Facciamo alla romana? — Sì, trenta euro a testa.
phrases.exEn: Shall we split it? — Yes, thirty euros each.

units.title: La mia giornata
units.intro: How to describe your daily routine, tell the time, name the days of the week and say how often you do things.

words.ex: La sveglia suona alle sette.
words.exEn: The alarm goes off at seven.

words.ex: Faccio la doccia la mattina.
words.exEn: I have a shower in the morning.
words.note: fare la doccia = to have/take a shower.

words.ex: Mi lavo i denti dopo colazione.
words.exEn: I brush my teeth after breakfast.
words.note: Italians “wash” their teeth: lavarsi i denti.

words.ex: Ho dimenticato lo spazzolino!
words.exEn: I forgot my toothbrush!

words.ex: La domenica resto in pigiama.
words.exEn: On Sundays I stay in my pyjamas.
words.note: Masculine and singular: il pigiama is one pair.

words.ex: Si fa la barba ogni mattina.
words.exEn: He shaves every morning.
words.note: farsi la barba = to shave. Colloquially, che barba! = how boring!

words.ex: Vado in palestra dopo il lavoro.
words.exEn: I go to the gym after work.

words.ex: Arrivo in ufficio alle nove.
words.exEn: I get to the office at nine.

words.ex: I bambini entrano a scuola alle otto.
words.exEn: The children start school at eight.

words.ex: Facciamo una pausa caffè?
words.exEn: Shall we take a coffee break?

words.ex: Il sabato faccio la spesa.
words.exEn: On Saturdays I do the food shopping.
words.note: fare la spesa = food shopping; fare shopping = shopping for fun.

words.ex: Alle quattro i bambini fanno merenda.
words.exEn: At four the kids have their afternoon snack.

words.ex: A metà mattina faccio uno spuntino.
words.exEn: Mid-morning I have a snack.

words.ex: Stasera ho tanto sonno.
words.exEn: I'm really sleepy tonight.
words.note: avere sonno = to be sleepy. Don't confuse with sogno (dream).

words.ex: Dopo pranzo faccio un pisolino.
words.exEn: After lunch I take a nap.

words.ex: Ho l'abitudine di leggere a letto.
words.exEn: I'm in the habit of reading in bed.
words.note: Feminine despite the -e: una buona abitudine.

words.ex: La mattina c'è sempre traffico.
words.exEn: There's always traffic in the morning.

words.ex: Scusa, vado di fretta.
words.exEn: Sorry, I'm in a rush.
words.note: avere fretta = to be in a hurry.

words.ex: Questa settimana ho il turno di notte.
words.exEn: This week I'm on the night shift.

words.ex: Il mio orologio è avanti.
words.exEn: My watch is fast.

words.ex: Arrivo tra cinque minuti.
words.exEn: I'll be there in five minutes.

words.ex: Sono le sei e un quarto.
words.exEn: It's a quarter past six.

words.ex: Ci vediamo alle due e mezza.
words.exEn: See you at half past two.
words.note: For time you can say e mezza or e mezzo; both are fine.

words.ex: Pranziamo a mezzogiorno.
words.exEn: We have lunch at noon.
words.note: No article for the time: è mezzogiorno.

words.ex: Vado a dormire dopo mezzanotte.
words.exEn: I go to bed after midnight.

words.ex: Il treno parte alle otto in punto.
words.exEn: The train leaves at eight on the dot.

words.ex: Sono le nove meno dieci.
words.exEn: It's ten to nine.
words.note: Minutes before the hour: le otto meno un quarto = a quarter to eight.

words.ex: Qual è l'orario del negozio?
words.exEn: What are the shop's opening hours?
words.note: in orario = on time.

words.ex: Non ho tempo per la colazione.
words.exEn: I don't have time for breakfast.
words.note: Time in general is tempo; clock time is ora: che ora è?

words.ex: Domani mi alzo presto.
words.exEn: Tomorrow I'm getting up early.
words.note: A presto! = See you soon!

words.ex: È tardi, vado a casa.
words.exEn: It's late, I'm going home.
words.note: tardi = late in the day; in ritardo = late for something.

words.ex: Scusa il ritardo!
words.exEn: Sorry I'm late!
words.note: essere in ritardo = to be late.

words.ex: Sono arrivato in anticipo.
words.exEn: I arrived early.
words.note: in anticipo = early (before the agreed time).

words.ex: Lavoro circa otto ore al giorno.
words.exEn: I work about eight hours a day.

words.ex: Che bella giornata!
words.exEn: What a lovely day!
words.note: giorno is the date or unit; giornata is the day as you live it: Buona giornata!

words.ex: Ho passato la mattinata in ufficio.
words.exEn: I spent the morning at the office.

words.ex: Il pomeriggio studio in biblioteca.
words.exEn: In the afternoon I study at the library.

words.en: evening (as a span of time); night out
words.ex: Grazie per la bella serata!
words.exEn: Thanks for a lovely evening!

words.ex: Stamattina ho perso l'autobus.
words.exEn: This morning I missed the bus.

words.ex: Cosa fai stasera?
words.exEn: What are you doing tonight?

words.ex: Stanotte non ho dormito bene.
words.exEn: I didn't sleep well last night.
words.note: Can mean the coming night or the one just gone — the tense tells you which.

words.ex: Parto dopodomani.
words.exEn: I'm leaving the day after tomorrow.

words.ex: L'ho visto l'altro ieri.
words.exEn: I saw him the day before yesterday.

words.ex: Nel weekend dormo fino a tardi.
words.exEn: At the weekend I sleep in.
words.note: Also il fine settimana.

words.ex: Il museo apre solo nei giorni feriali.
words.exEn: The museum only opens on weekdays.
words.note: Trap: feriale means a working day, not a holiday.

words.ex: Nei giorni festivi l'autobus non passa.
words.exEn: The bus doesn't run on Sundays and holidays.

words.ex: Il lunedì vado in piscina.
words.exEn: On Mondays I go swimming.
words.note: Days are lowercase. With il it means “every”: il lunedì = on Mondays; lunedì alone = this Monday.

words.ex: Martedì ho un appuntamento.
words.exEn: I have an appointment on Tuesday.

words.ex: Il mercoledì lavoro da casa.
words.exEn: On Wednesdays I work from home.

words.ex: Ci vediamo giovedì sera?
words.exEn: Shall we meet Thursday evening?

words.ex: Finalmente è venerdì!
words.exEn: It's Friday at last!

words.ex: Il sabato mattina faccio sport.
words.exEn: On Saturday mornings I do sport.

words.ex: La domenica pranziamo dai nonni.
words.exEn: On Sundays we have lunch at our grandparents'.
words.note: The only feminine day.

words.ex: Domani è festa, i negozi sono chiusi.
words.exEn: Tomorrow is a holiday, the shops are closed.

words.ex: Di solito mi alzo alle sette.
words.exEn: I usually get up at seven.

words.ex: Esco spesso con i colleghi.
words.exEn: I often go out with my colleagues.

words.ex: Qualche volta cucino io.
words.exEn: Sometimes I do the cooking.
words.note: qualche is always followed by a singular noun. Also a volte.

words.ex: Ogni tanto prendo un taxi.
words.exEn: Every now and then I take a taxi.

words.ex: Raramente guardo la TV.
words.exEn: I rarely watch TV.

words.ex: Quasi ogni giorno vado a piedi.
words.exEn: I walk almost every day.

words.ex: Chiamo mia madre ogni domenica.
words.exEn: I call my mother every Sunday.
words.note: Never changes and always takes a singular noun: ogni giorno.

words.ex: Vado in palestra tre volte a settimana.
words.exEn: I go to the gym three times a week.
words.note: Counting times = volta; clock time = ora; time in general = tempo.

words.ex: Normalmente pranzo all'una.
words.exEn: Normally I have lunch at one.

words.ex: Faccio la doccia e poi mi vesto.
words.exEn: I take a shower and then I get dressed.

words.ex: Infine, vado a letto verso mezzanotte.
words.exEn: Finally, I go to bed around midnight.
words.note: infine = last in a list; finalmente = at last (with relief).

words.ex: Mi alzo subito, non resto a letto.
words.exEn: I get up straight away, I don't lie in bed.

words.ex: Torno verso le sette.
words.exEn: I'll be back around seven.

words.ex: Lavoro fino alle sei.
words.exEn: I work until six.

words.ex: Lavoro qui da tre anni.
words.exEn: I've been working here for three years.
words.note: da + present = “have been doing for”: studio da un mese. Also dalle nove alle cinque = from nine to five.

words.ex: Sei già sveglia?
words.exEn: Are you awake already?

words.ex: Sei pronto? Usciamo!
words.exEn: Are you ready? Let's go!
words.note: Italians answer the phone with Pronto?

words.ex: Sei libero domani pomeriggio?
words.exEn: Are you free tomorrow afternoon?
words.note: Free of commitments, not free of charge (that's gratis).

words.ex: Oggi sono molto occupata.
words.exEn: I'm very busy today.

words.ex: La domenica sono un po' pigro.
words.exEn: On Sundays I'm a bit lazy.

words.ex: Mia sorella è molto mattiniera.
words.exEn: My sister is a real morning person.

words.ex: Oggi è una giornata tranquilla.
words.exEn: Today is a quiet day.
words.note: Tranquillo! also means “Don't worry!”

words.ex: È stata una giornata lunga.
words.exEn: It's been a long day.
words.note: Plural: lunghi, lunghe.

words.ex: Il mio capo è sempre puntuale.
words.exEn: My boss is always on time.

words.ex: Il lunedì è sempre faticoso.
words.exEn: Mondays are always tiring.

words.ex: Faccio una colazione veloce.
words.exEn: I have a quick breakfast.

verbs.note: Reflexive when you wake up yourself; svegliare (non-reflexive) = to wake someone else: mi svegli alle sette?
ex: Mi sveglio sempre prima della sveglia.
I always wake up before the alarm.
A che ora vi siete svegliati?
What time did you wake up?

verbs.en: to get up; to stand up
verbs.note: svegliarsi is opening your eyes, alzarsi is getting out of bed. Non-reflexive alzare = to raise, lift: alzare la mano.
ex: Mi alzo alle sei e mezza.
I get up at half past six.

verbs.note: vestirsi bene = to dress well; vestirsi da = to dress up as. Non-reflexive vestire = to dress someone: vesto i bambini.
ex: I get dressed in five minutes.
Si è vestita di nero per la festa.
She wore black for the party.

verbs.en: to go out; to leave; to come out
verbs.note: uscire di casa = to leave the house; uscire con qualcuno = to go out with someone. Stem changes to esc- when stressed: esco, but usciamo.
ex: I leave the house at eight.
Ieri sera siamo usciti con gli amici.
Last night we went out with friends.

verbs.en: to come back; to return; to go back
verbs.note: tornare a casa = to go/come home. Also used for “again”: torno a lavorare = I go back to work.
ex: What time are you back tonight?

verbs.note: andare a dormire = to go to bed. Dormire fino a tardi = to sleep in. A model for regular -ire verbs without -isc-.
ex: I sleep eight hours a night.

verbs.note: cominciare a + infinitive: comincio a lavorare. When the subject is the event itself, it takes essere: il film è cominciato.

verbs.en: to have to; must; to owe
verbs.note: Followed directly by an infinitive: devo andare. Dovrei = I should. With a noun it means “to owe”: ti devo dieci euro.
ex: Tomorrow I have to get up early.

phrases.note: Also Che ora è? — both are correct.
phrases.ex: Scusi, che ore sono? — Sono le tre e dieci.
phrases.exEn: Excuse me, what time is it? — It's ten past three.

phrases.lit: They are the eight and half
phrases.note: Plural sono le because “hours” is understood.
phrases.ex: Sono già le otto e mezza? Sono in ritardo!
phrases.exEn: Is it half eight already? I'm late!

phrases.note: Singular for one o'clock, like è mezzogiorno and è mezzanotte.
phrases.ex: Andiamo a pranzo? È l'una.
phrases.exEn: Shall we go for lunch? It's one o'clock.

phrases.ex: A che ora apre la farmacia? — Alle nove.
phrases.exEn: What time does the chemist's open? — At nine.

phrases.ex: Dove sei? — Faccio la doccia, arrivo!
phrases.exEn: Where are you? — I'm in the shower, coming!

phrases.ex: Vado a letto, ho sonno. — Buonanotte!
phrases.exEn: I'm off to bed, I'm sleepy. — Good night!

phrases.ex: Che giornata! Sono distrutto.
phrases.exEn: What a day! I'm exhausted.

phrases.note: Only when going to bed or leaving late at night; otherwise say buonasera.
phrases.ex: Buonanotte, a domani! — Notte!
phrases.exEn: Good night, see you tomorrow! — Night!

phrases.ex: Sono in ritardo, scusa! — Tranquillo, ti aspetto.
phrases.exEn: I'm late, sorry! — Don't worry, I'll wait for you.

phrases.ex: Ho fretta, ti chiamo dopo.
phrases.exEn: I'm in a hurry, I'll call you later.

units.title: A casa
units.intro: How to name the rooms, furniture and everyday objects in your home, describe it, and say where things are.

words.ex: Abito in un appartamento piccolo.
words.exEn: I live in a small flat.

words.ex: La casa ha quattro stanze.
words.exEn: The house has four rooms.
words.note: Any room is a stanza; camera usually means bedroom.

words.ex: La sera stiamo in soggiorno.
words.exEn: In the evening we sit in the living room.

words.ex: Il divano è in salotto.
words.exEn: The sofa is in the lounge.

words.ex: Lavoro nello studio, vicino alla finestra.
words.exEn: I work in the study, by the window.

words.ex: Lascia le scarpe all'ingresso.
words.exEn: Leave your shoes in the hall.

words.ex: Il bagno è in fondo al corridoio.
words.exEn: The bathroom is at the end of the corridor.

words.ex: Facciamo colazione sul balcone.
words.exEn: We have breakfast on the balcony.

words.ex: I bambini giocano in giardino.
words.exEn: The children are playing in the garden.

words.ex: La bici è in garage.
words.exEn: The bike is in the garage.

words.ex: Metto le scatole in cantina.
words.exEn: I put the boxes in the cellar.
words.note: False friend: not a canteen. A canteen is la mensa.

words.ex: Salgo le scale a piedi.
words.exEn: I walk up the stairs.
words.note: Usually plural for a staircase: le scale.

words.ex: Abitiamo al secondo piano.
words.exEn: We live on the second floor.
words.note: piano terra = ground floor. As an adverb, piano = slowly, quietly.

words.ex: L'ascensore è rotto di nuovo.
words.exEn: The lift is broken again.

words.ex: Le pareti sono bianche.
words.exEn: The walls are white.
words.note: Inside walls are pareti; outside or garden walls are muri.

words.ex: Il pavimento è di legno.
words.exEn: The floor is wooden.
words.note: The surface you walk on; a level of a building is piano.

words.ex: Questi mobili sono della nonna.
words.exEn: This furniture was my grandmother's.
words.note: Countable: un mobile, i mobili = furniture. Not a phone (that's cellulare).

words.ex: Il gatto dorme sul divano.
words.exEn: The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

words.ex: Leggo sempre in poltrona.
words.exEn: I always read in the armchair.

words.ex: I vestiti sono nell'armadio.
words.exEn: The clothes are in the wardrobe.

words.ex: La scrivania è piena di carte.
words.exEn: The desk is covered in papers.

words.ex: Ho una libreria enorme in salotto.
words.exEn: I have a huge bookcase in the lounge.
words.note: False friend: a library is la biblioteca.

words.ex: Il libro è sullo scaffale in alto.
words.exEn: The book is on the top shelf.

words.ex: Il telefono è sul comodino.
words.exEn: The phone is on the bedside table.

words.ex: Le forbici sono nel primo cassetto.
words.exEn: The scissors are in the top drawer.

words.ex: C'è uno specchio grande nell'ingresso.
words.exEn: There's a big mirror in the hall.

words.ex: Accendi la lampada, per favore.
words.exEn: Turn on the lamp, please.

words.ex: Abbiamo un tappeto rosso in camera.
words.exEn: We have a red rug in the bedroom.

words.ex: Chiudi le tende, c'è troppo sole.
words.exEn: Close the curtains, it's too sunny.

words.ex: Mettiamo il quadro sopra il divano?
words.exEn: Shall we put the painting above the sofa?

words.ex: Il latte è in frigorifero.
words.exEn: The milk is in the fridge.
words.note: Usually shortened to il frigo (plural i frigo).

words.ex: La torta è nel forno.
words.exEn: The cake is in the oven.

words.ex: Scaldo la pasta nel microonde.
words.exEn: I heat up the pasta in the microwave.

words.ex: Hai spento il fornello?
words.exEn: Did you turn off the hob?

words.ex: La lavatrice è in bagno.
words.exEn: The washing machine is in the bathroom.
words.note: In Italy it's often in the bathroom, not the kitchen.

words.ex: Metti i piatti in lavastoviglie.
words.exEn: Put the plates in the dishwasher.

words.ex: Il lavandino è pieno di piatti.
words.exEn: The sink is full of dishes.

words.ex: In camera non abbiamo la televisione.
words.exEn: We don't have a TV in the bedroom.
words.note: Often just la tv (said ti-vù) or la tele.

words.ex: Il computer è sulla scrivania.
words.exEn: The computer is on the desk.
words.note: Foreign words don't change in the plural.

words.ex: Puoi accendere la luce?
words.exEn: Can you turn on the light?
words.note: la bolletta della luce = the electricity bill.

words.ex: Il riscaldamento non funziona.
words.exEn: The heating isn't working.

words.ex: D'estate il condizionatore è sempre acceso.
words.exEn: In summer the air conditioner is always on.

words.ex: Ho troppe cose in casa.
words.exEn: I have too many things at home.
words.note: Also a question word: Cosa fai? = What are you doing?

words.ex: Mi piace dormire con due cuscini.
words.exEn: I like sleeping with two pillows.

words.ex: Hai una coperta in più?
words.exEn: Do you have a spare blanket?

words.ex: Cambio le lenzuola ogni settimana.
words.exEn: I change the sheets every week.
words.note: Irregular plural that turns feminine: le lenzuola.

words.ex: Gli asciugamani puliti sono in bagno.
words.exEn: The clean towels are in the bathroom.
words.note: Masculine, even though la mano is feminine.

words.ex: Manca il sapone in bagno.
words.exEn: There's no soap in the bathroom.

words.ex: Suona il campanello: chi è?
words.exEn: The doorbell's ringing: who is it?

words.ex: Butta la carta nel cestino.
words.exEn: Throw the paper in the bin.

words.ex: Le foto sono in una scatola.
words.exEn: The photos are in a box.
words.note: Stress on the first syllable: scàtola.

words.ex: Ho mille libri e poco spazio.
words.exEn: I have a thousand books and little space.

words.ex: Che bella foto sul frigo!
words.exEn: What a nice photo on the fridge!
words.note: Short for fotografia, so it's feminine and doesn't change in the plural.

words.ex: L'interruttore è dietro la porta.
words.exEn: The light switch is behind the door.

words.en: on; on top of; above; upstairs
words.ex: Le chiavi sono sopra il tavolo.
words.exEn: The keys are on the table.

words.ex: Il gatto è sotto il letto.
words.exEn: The cat is under the bed.

words.ex: Fa freddo, andiamo dentro.
words.exEn: It's cold, let's go inside.

words.ex: Il cane dorme fuori.
words.exEn: The dog sleeps outside.

words.ex: La macchina è davanti a casa.
words.exEn: The car is in front of the house.
words.note: Before a noun use davanti a.

words.ex: Il giardino è dietro la casa.
words.exEn: The garden is behind the house.

words.ex: La lampada è accanto al divano.
words.exEn: The lamp is next to the sofa.
words.note: Before a noun use accanto a.

words.ex: Abito vicino alla stazione.
words.exEn: I live near the station.
words.note: vicino a + place. As a noun, il vicino di casa = neighbour.

words.ex: Casa mia è lontano dal centro.
words.exEn: My house is far from the centre.
words.note: lontano da + place.

words.ex: La sedia è tra la finestra e l'armadio.
words.exEn: The chair is between the window and the wardrobe.
words.note: tra and fra are interchangeable. With time: tra un'ora = in an hour.

words.ex: Il libro è sul comodino.
words.exEn: The book is on the bedside table.
words.note: Merges with the article: sul, sulla, sullo, sui…

words.ex: Il bagno è di fronte alla cucina.
words.exEn: The bathroom is opposite the kitchen.
words.note: di fronte a + place.

words.ex: Il tavolo è in mezzo alla stanza.
words.exEn: The table is in the middle of the room.

words.ex: Nell'angolo c'è una pianta.
words.exEn: There's a plant in the corner.

words.ex: Il soggiorno è molto luminoso.
words.exEn: The living room is very bright.

words.ex: La cantina è buia.
words.exEn: The cellar is dark.
words.note: As a noun: il buio = the dark.

words.ex: Cerco un appartamento spazioso.
words.exEn: I'm looking for a spacious flat.

words.ex: Questo divano è comodissimo.
words.exEn: This sofa is really comfortable.
words.note: Stress on the first syllable: còmodo. Also “handy”: la casa è comoda per la stazione.

words.ex: Hai una casa molto accogliente.
words.exEn: You have a really cosy home.

words.ex: La cucina è moderna.
words.exEn: The kitchen is modern.

words.ex: Affittano un monolocale arredato.
words.exEn: They're renting out a furnished studio flat.

words.ex: La casa è pulita per la festa.
words.exEn: The house is clean for the party.

words.ex: I piatti sono ancora sporchi.
words.exEn: The plates are still dirty.
words.note: Plural: sporchi, sporche.

words.ex: La strada qui è rumorosa.
words.exEn: The street here is noisy.

words.ex: L'affitto è di ottocento euro.
words.exEn: The rent is eight hundred euros.
words.note: essere in affitto = to rent (as a tenant).

words.ex: Dal balcone c'è una vista stupenda.
words.exEn: There's a stunning view from the balcony.

verbs.note: Also takes essere (sono vissuto a Roma); both are correct. vivere is about life in general; abitare is only about where you live.
ex: Vivo da sola in un piccolo appartamento.
I live alone in a small flat.
Abbiamo vissuto dieci anni a Napoli.
We lived in Naples for ten years.

verbs.en: to put; to place; to put on (clothes)
verbs.note: Irregular participle messo. mettere in ordine = to tidy up; mettersi = to put on (clothes).
ex: Where shall I put your jacket?
Ho messo il latte in frigo.
I put the milk in the fridge.

verbs.note: Regular in the present, but the participle is aperto. aperto is also the adjective “open”: il negozio è aperto.
ex: Can you open the window? It's hot.

verbs.en: to close; to shut; to lock
verbs.note: Irregular participle chiuso, also the adjective “closed”. chiudere a chiave = to lock.
ex: Chiudi la porta a chiave, per favore.

verbs.en: to enter; to go in; to come in
verbs.note: Always entrare in + place (never a direct object): entro in casa. Posso entrare? = May I come in?
ex: Entra pure, la porta è aperta!
Come on in, the door's open!
We went into the living room.

verbs.note: cucinare = to cook (a meal); for the cooking process itself Italians also use cuocere. Chi cucina stasera?
ex: Mio padre ha cucinato le lasagne.

verbs.note: To leave something behind, not to depart (that's partire or uscire). lasciare + infinitive = to let: lasciami dormire.
ex: Ho lasciato le chiavi a casa.
I've left my keys at home.
Lascia la luce accesa, per favore.

verbs.note: trovare also means “to think, find (an opinion)”: trovo che sia bello. andare a trovare = to visit a person.
ex: Abbiamo trovato casa vicino al centro.
We found a place near the centre.

phrases.note: Said when stepping into someone's home. Reply: Avanti! or Prego!
phrases.ex: Permesso? — Avanti, entra pure!
phrases.exEn: May I come in? — Come in, come in!

phrases.en: Come in and sit down! / Make yourself comfortable!
phrases.note: Formal: Si accomodi!
phrases.ex: Ciao Anna, accomodati! — Grazie, che bella casa!
phrases.exEn: Hi Anna, come in and sit down! — Thanks, what a lovely home!

phrases.it: Fai come se fossi a casa tua
phrases.lit: Do as if you were at your house
phrases.ex: Fai come se fossi a casa tua. — Grazie, sei gentile.
phrases.exEn: Make yourself at home. — Thanks, that's kind of you.

phrases.ex: Che bella casa! È tutto nuovo? — Sì, l'abbiamo rifatta.
phrases.exEn: What a lovely home! Is it all new? — Yes, we redid it.

phrases.note: The owner says affitto la casa (I rent it out).
phrases.ex: La casa è tua? — No, sono in affitto.
phrases.exEn: Is the house yours? — No, I'm renting.

phrases.en: I live on the third floor
phrases.lit: I live at the third floor
phrases.note: Italian floors start at piano terra, so the primo piano is one up.
phrases.ex: Abito al terzo piano, senza ascensore. — Che fatica!
phrases.exEn: I live on the third floor, with no lift. — How tiring!

phrases.ex: Finalmente! Casa dolce casa.
phrases.exEn: At last! Home sweet home.

phrases.note: For a feminine thing: Dove l'hai messa?
phrases.ex: Dov'è il caricabatterie? Dove l'hai messo? — Nel cassetto.
phrases.exEn: Where's the charger? Where did you put it? — In the drawer.

phrases.ex: Non trovo più gli occhiali! — Sono sulla tua testa.
phrases.exEn: I can't find my glasses! — They're on your head.

phrases.en: Here it is! / There it is!
phrases.note: ecco + pronoun: eccola (f), eccoli (m pl), eccomi (here I am).
phrases.ex: Hai visto il telecomando? — Eccolo, sul divano!
phrases.exEn: Have you seen the remote? — Here it is, on the sofa!

units.title: In città
units.intro: How to name places and shops in town, get around by public transport, ask for and give directions, and buy tickets.

words.ex: Vado in centro a fare un giro.
words.exEn: I'm going into town for a wander.
words.note: in centro = downtown, in/to the town centre.

words.ex: Ci vediamo in piazza alle sei.
words.exEn: Let's meet in the square at six.

words.ex: Il mio quartiere è molto tranquillo.
words.exEn: My neighbourhood is very quiet.

words.ex: Abitano in periferia, lontano dal centro.
words.exEn: They live on the outskirts, far from the centre.

words.ex: Ci sono bar in questa zona?
words.exEn: Are there any cafés in this area?
words.note: ZTL (zona a traffico limitato): a restricted-traffic zone — don't drive in!

words.ex: Il museo è in fondo al viale.
words.exEn: The museum is at the end of the avenue.

words.ex: Attraversiamo il ponte a piedi.
words.exEn: Let's walk across the bridge.
words.note: Also a long weekend: fare il ponte = take the day off between a holiday and the weekend.

words.ex: Abito in quel palazzo giallo.
words.exEn: I live in that yellow building.
words.note: Not only a palace: any large building is a palazzo.

words.ex: La chiesa è aperta la mattina.
words.exEn: The church is open in the morning.

words.ex: Il museo è gratis la prima domenica del mese.
words.exEn: The museum is free on the first Sunday of the month.

words.ex: Corro nel parco ogni mattina.
words.exEn: I go running in the park every morning.

words.ex: L'acqua della fontana è buona.
words.exEn: The water from the fountain is good to drink.

words.ex: La stazione è a dieci minuti da qui.
words.exEn: The station is ten minutes from here.

words.ex: L'ospedale è vicino al parco.
words.exEn: The hospital is near the park.

words.ex: Il municipio è in piazza.
words.exEn: The town hall is in the square.
words.note: Also called il comune.

words.ex: Andiamo al cinema stasera?
words.exEn: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?
words.note: Short for cinematografo, so masculine and unchanged in the plural.

words.ex: Il teatro è dietro la chiesa.
words.exEn: The theatre is behind the church.

words.ex: Studio in biblioteca il pomeriggio.
words.exEn: I study at the library in the afternoon.
words.note: False friend: a bookshop is la libreria.

words.ex: I negozi chiudono alle otto.
words.exEn: The shops close at eight.
words.note: Many small shops close for lunch, roughly 13:00–16:00.

words.ex: C'è un supermercato qui vicino?
words.exEn: Is there a supermarket near here?

words.ex: La farmacia è all'angolo.
words.exEn: The chemist's is on the corner.
words.note: Look for the green cross. Stress on the -ì-: farmacìa.

words.ex: Compro il giornale in edicola.
words.exEn: I buy the paper at the newsstand.

words.ex: I biglietti dell'autobus si comprano in tabaccheria.
words.exEn: You buy bus tickets at the tobacconist's.
words.note: Look for the big T sign. They sell bus tickets, stamps and phone top-ups too.

words.ex: La domenica passo in pasticceria.
words.exEn: On Sundays I stop by the pastry shop.

words.ex: La gelateria in piazza è la migliore.
words.exEn: The ice-cream shop in the square is the best.

words.ex: La banca apre alle otto e mezza.
words.exEn: The bank opens at half past eight.

words.ex: Scusi, c'è un bancomat qui vicino?
words.exEn: Excuse me, is there a cash machine near here?

words.ex: Devo andare in posta a spedire un pacco.
words.exEn: I need to go to the post office to send a parcel.
words.note: Short for l'ufficio postale.

words.ex: Mi fermo dal benzinaio.
words.exEn: I'll stop at the petrol station.

words.ex: Prendo l'autobus per andare al lavoro.
words.exEn: I take the bus to work.
words.note: Often just il bus. Unchanged in the plural.

words.ex: Il tram passa ogni dieci minuti.
words.exEn: The tram comes every ten minutes.

words.ex: In metropolitana si fa prima.
words.exEn: It's quicker by underground.
words.note: Usually shortened to la metro.

words.ex: Il treno per Milano è in ritardo.
words.exEn: The train to Milan is late.

words.ex: Chiamiamo un taxi?
words.exEn: Shall we call a taxi?

words.ex: Vado al lavoro in macchina.
words.exEn: I drive to work.
words.note: Means of transport take in: in macchina, in treno, in bici — but a piedi.

words.ex: Ho parcheggiato l'auto in piazza.
words.exEn: I parked the car in the square.
words.note: Short for automobile, so it's feminine and unchanged in the plural.

words.ex: In città mi muovo in bici.
words.exEn: I get around town by bike.
words.note: Short for bicicletta.

words.ex: Con il motorino non trovo traffico.
words.exEn: On my scooter I avoid the traffic.

words.ex: Molti ragazzi usano il monopattino elettrico.
words.exEn: Lots of young people use e-scooters.

words.ex: Scendo alla prossima fermata.
words.exEn: I'm getting off at the next stop.

words.ex: Il treno parte dal binario tre.
words.exEn: The train leaves from platform three.

words.ex: Prendi la linea rossa della metro.
words.exEn: Take the red line on the underground.

words.ex: Non trovo parcheggio in centro.
words.exEn: I can't find parking in the centre.

words.ex: Devo fare benzina.
words.exEn: I need to get petrol.
words.note: fare benzina = to fill up.

words.ex: L'autista è stato gentilissimo.
words.exEn: The driver was really kind.
words.note: Same form for men and women: l'autista. A person driving their own car is il/la conducente or just “chi guida”.

words.ex: Questa via è solo per i pedoni.
words.exEn: This street is for pedestrians only.

words.ex: Vado a scuola a piedi.
words.exEn: I walk to school.

words.ex: Gira a destra al semaforo.
words.exEn: Turn right at the lights.
words.note: a destra = on/to the right.

words.ex: La farmacia è sulla sinistra.
words.exEn: The chemist's is on the left.

words.ex: Vada sempre dritto.
words.exEn: Keep going straight ahead.
words.note: Also spelled diritto.

words.ex: Al primo incrocio giri a sinistra.
words.exEn: At the first junction turn left.

words.ex: Dopo il semaforo c'è la banca.
words.exEn: The bank is after the traffic lights.
words.note: Singular in Italian: il semaforo è rosso = the lights are red.

words.ex: Alla rotonda prenda la seconda uscita.
words.exEn: At the roundabout take the second exit.

words.ex: Cammina sul marciapiede!
words.exEn: Walk on the pavement!

words.ex: Guardo la mappa sul telefono.
words.exEn: I'm checking the map on my phone.
words.note: A paper street map is often called la piantina or la cartina.

words.ex: Mi può dare un'indicazione?
words.exEn: Could you give me directions?
words.note: Usually plural: le indicazioni = directions; road signs.

words.ex: Facciamo un giro in centro?
words.exEn: Shall we take a stroll around town?
words.note: fare un giro = to go for a wander, drive or ride.

words.ex: Passiamo attraverso il parco.
words.exEn: Let's go through the park.

words.ex: La fermata è laggiù, vicino al bar.
words.exEn: The stop is over there, near the café.

words.ex: Vieni qua, ti faccio vedere.
words.exEn: Come here, I'll show you.
words.note: qua and qui mean the same; là = there.

words.ex: Dov'è l'uscita della metro?
words.exEn: Where's the way out of the underground?

words.ex: L'entrata del museo è sul retro.
words.exEn: The museum entrance is at the back.

words.ex: Siamo persi, chiediamo a qualcuno.
words.exEn: We're lost, let's ask someone.

words.ex: Il bar è a cento metri.
words.exEn: The café is a hundred metres away.
words.note: Gender trap: il metro = the metre, la metro = the underground.

words.ex: L'aeroporto è a venti chilometri.
words.exEn: The airport is twenty kilometres away.
words.note: Stress on -lò-: chilòmetro.

words.ex: Ho comprato il biglietto online.
words.exEn: I bought the ticket online.
words.note: Remember to validate it (timbrare) on buses and regional trains.

words.ex: La biglietteria è chiusa, uso la macchinetta.
words.exEn: The ticket office is closed, I'll use the machine.

words.ex: Ho l'abbonamento mensile dell'autobus.
words.exEn: I have a monthly bus pass.

words.ex: Un biglietto di sola andata, per favore.
words.exEn: A one-way ticket, please.
words.note: andata e ritorno = return / round trip.

words.ex: Il ritorno è alle sei.
words.exEn: The return journey is at six.

words.ex: L'ultima corsa è a mezzanotte.
words.exEn: The last bus is at midnight.
words.note: di corsa = in a rush.

words.ex: Ho perso la coincidenza a Bologna.
words.exEn: I missed my connection in Bologna.

words.ex: Domani c'è sciopero dei treni.
words.exEn: There's a train strike tomorrow.
words.note: Strikes are announced in advance — always check before you travel.

words.ex: Il controllore chiede i biglietti.
words.exEn: The inspector is checking tickets.

words.ex: Senza biglietto prendi la multa.
words.exEn: Without a ticket you get fined.

words.ex: Per gli studenti c'è il biglietto ridotto.
words.exEn: There's a reduced ticket for students.

words.ex: Un biglietto intero costa dodici euro.
words.exEn: A full-price ticket costs twelve euros.

words.ex: Per i bambini il museo è gratis.
words.exEn: The museum is free for children.
words.note: Never changes form. Also gratuito (adj).

words.ex: Il prossimo treno parte tra dieci minuti.
words.exEn: The next train leaves in ten minutes.
words.note: Stress on the first syllable: pròssimo.

words.ex: Ho perso l'ultimo autobus.
words.exEn: I missed the last bus.

verbs.en: to arrive; to get (somewhere); to reach
verbs.note: arrivare a + city/small place, arrivare in + country or big area (arrivo in stazione). Arrivo! = Coming!
ex: A che ora arriva il treno?
What time does the train arrive?
Siamo arrivati a Roma ieri sera.
We arrived in Rome last night.

verbs.en: to leave; to depart; to set off
verbs.note: partire da = to leave from, partire per = to leave for: parto da Milano per Napoli. To leave a thing behind is lasciare.
ex: Il treno parte dal binario due.
The train leaves from platform two.
Sono partita per Londra a giugno.
I left for London in June.

verbs.en: to look for; to search; to try (to)
verbs.note: No “for” in Italian: cerco la stazione = I'm looking for the station. cercare di + infinitive = to try to. An h keeps the c hard: cerchi, cercherò.
ex: Scusi, cerco la fermata del tram.
Excuse me, I'm looking for the tram stop.
I try to arrive on time.

verbs.en: to go up; to get on (a vehicle); to climb
verbs.note: salire su = to get on/in: salgo sull'autobus. With a direct object it takes avere: ho salito le scale.
ex: Let's get on the tram here.
È salita al quinto piano a piedi.
She walked up to the fifth floor.

verbs.en: to go down; to get off (a vehicle); to come down
verbs.note: scendere da = to get off: scendo dal treno. Irregular participle sceso. With a direct object it takes avere: ho sceso le scale.
ex: Where are you getting off? — At the next one.
We got off at Piazza Duomo.

verbs.note: No “for” in Italian: aspetto l'autobus = I'm waiting for the bus. Aspetta! = Wait!
ex: I'll wait for you outside the cinema.
We waited half an hour for the tram.

verbs.note: camminare describes the activity of walking; to say you go somewhere on foot use andare a piedi. A stroll is una passeggiata.
ex: I like walking around the centre.

verbs.en: to drive; to guide; to lead
verbs.note: guidare = to drive (a vehicle); to go somewhere by car is andare in macchina. la patente = driving licence.
ex: I never drive in the city.

phrases.note: Informal: Scusa, dov'è…? For plural: dove sono…?
phrases.ex: Scusi, dov'è la stazione? — Sempre dritto, poi a destra.
phrases.exEn: Excuse me, where's the station? — Straight on, then right.

phrases.ex: Scusi, per andare al Colosseo? — Prenda la metro B.
phrases.exEn: Excuse me, how do I get to the Colosseum? — Take metro line B.

phrases.ex: Il museo è lontano? — No, sono cinque minuti.
phrases.exEn: Is the museum far? — No, it's five minutes.

phrases.it: Mi sono perso / Mi sono persa
phrases.note: Men say perso, women persa.
phrases.ex: Scusi, mi sono persa. Dove siamo? — In via Dante.
phrases.exEn: Excuse me, I'm lost. Where are we? — On Via Dante.

phrases.note: sempre here means “keep going”, not “always”.
phrases.ex: La piazza? Sempre dritto, non può sbagliare.
phrases.exEn: The square? Straight on, you can't miss it.

phrases.note: Informal: gira a destra / a sinistra.
phrases.ex: Al semaforo giri a destra, e c'è la farmacia.
phrases.exEn: Turn right at the lights, and there's the chemist's.

phrases.it: È a cinque minuti a piedi
phrases.lit: It's at five minutes on foot
phrases.ex: La spiaggia è a cinque minuti a piedi. — Perfetto!
phrases.exEn: The beach is a five-minute walk. — Perfect!

phrases.ex: Un biglietto per Firenze, per favore. — Andata e ritorno?
phrases.exEn: A ticket to Florence, please. — Return?

phrases.en: I'm getting off at the next stop
phrases.note: On a crowded bus, say Permesso! to get past people.
phrases.ex: Permesso, scendo alla prossima! — Prego.
phrases.exEn: Excuse me, I'm getting off at the next stop! — Go ahead.

phrases.ex: Perché non passa l'autobus? — Oggi c'è sciopero.
phrases.exEn: Why isn't the bus coming? — There's a strike today.

units.title: Fare acquisti
units.intro: Clothes, colours, sizes and prices, plus how to buy things in shops and at the market.

words.ex: Questo vestito rosso è bellissimo.
words.exEn: This red dress is beautiful.
words.note: For men, vestito usually means a suit; vestiti (pl) = clothes in general.

words.ex: Ho comprato una maglietta bianca.
words.exEn: I bought a white T-shirt.

words.ex: Porti la camicia anche d'estate?
words.exEn: Do you wear a shirt in summer too?
words.note: Plural keeps the i: camicie. Don't confuse with camino (fireplace).

words.ex: Questi pantaloni sono troppo lunghi.
words.exEn: These trousers are too long.
words.note: Usually plural, like English trousers.

words.ex: Cerco una gonna nera, corta.
words.exEn: I'm looking for a short black skirt.

words.ex: Prendi la giacca, stasera fa fresco.
words.exEn: Take your jacket, it's cool tonight.

words.ex: Mi serve un cappotto per l'inverno.
words.exEn: I need a coat for the winter.

words.ex: Il maglione di lana è caldo.
words.exEn: The wool sweater is warm.

words.ex: Queste scarpe mi fanno male.
words.exEn: These shoes hurt my feet.

words.ex: Metto sempre i jeans.
words.exEn: I always wear jeans.
words.note: Foreign word: never changes.

words.ex: Ho un buco nel calzino.
words.exEn: I've got a hole in my sock.

words.ex: Ti sta bene quel cappello!
words.exEn: That hat suits you!

words.ex: Ho dimenticato la borsa in negozio.
words.exEn: I left my bag in the shop.

words.ex: È una sciarpa di seta.
words.exEn: It's a silk scarf.

words.ex: La cintura marrone va bene con le scarpe.
words.exEn: The brown belt goes well with the shoes.

words.ex: La domenica sto in felpa.
words.exEn: On Sundays I just wear a sweatshirt.

words.ex: Ho bisogno di un costume nuovo per il mare.
words.exEn: I need a new swimsuit for the beach.
words.note: Short for costume da bagno.

words.ex: Dove ho messo gli occhiali da sole?
words.exEn: Where did I put my sunglasses?
words.note: Always plural. Occhiali da sole = sunglasses.

words.ex: Questi stivali sono di pelle.
words.exEn: These boots are leather.

words.ex: Vorrei la stessa borsa, ma rossa.
words.exEn: I'd like the same bag, but red.

words.ex: Ha una giacca blu.
words.exEn: She has a navy jacket.
words.note: Invariable: i pantaloni blu, le scarpe blu.

words.ex: Il cielo è azzurro oggi.
words.exEn: The sky is blue today.
words.note: Italians see blu and azzurro as two different colours. The national teams are gli Azzurri.

words.ex: Preferisco il maglione verde.
words.exEn: I prefer the green sweater.

words.ex: Il giallo non mi sta bene.
words.exEn: Yellow doesn't suit me.

words.ex: Il nero va sempre di moda.
words.exEn: Black is always in fashion.

words.ex: Cerco una camicia bianca.
words.exEn: I'm looking for a white shirt.
words.note: Plural: bianchi, bianche.

words.ex: Ho un cappotto grigio scuro.
words.exEn: I have a dark grey coat.
words.note: Feminine plural: grigie.

words.ex: Le piace molto il rosa.
words.exEn: She really likes pink.
words.note: Invariable as a colour: le magliette rosa. As a noun, la rosa is a rose.

words.ex: Ha gli stivali marroni.
words.exEn: He has brown boots.

words.ex: La maglietta arancione è in offerta.
words.exEn: The orange T-shirt is on offer.
words.note: The fruit is l'arancia.

words.ex: Ha una sciarpa viola.
words.exEn: She has a purple scarf.
words.note: Invariable: le gonne viola.

words.ex: Il sabato vado al mercato.
words.exEn: On Saturdays I go to the market.

words.ex: Il prezzo è scritto sull'etichetta.
words.exEn: The price is on the label.

words.ex: I saldi cominciano a gennaio.
words.exEn: The sales start in January.
words.note: Usually plural. In saldo = on sale.

words.ex: C'è uno sconto del venti per cento.
words.exEn: There's a twenty percent discount.

words.ex: Che taglia porti? — La media.
words.exEn: What size are you? — Medium.

words.ex: Che numero di scarpe porti?
words.exEn: What shoe size are you?
words.note: For shoes Italians say numero, not taglia.

words.ex: Il camerino è in fondo a destra.
words.exEn: The fitting room is at the back on the right.

words.ex: Ho visto una giacca in vetrina.
words.exEn: I saw a jacket in the window.

words.ex: Vuole un sacchetto? Costa dieci centesimi.
words.exEn: Do you want a bag? It's ten cents.

words.ex: Ecco il resto, buona giornata.
words.exEn: Here's your change, have a nice day.

words.ex: Le mele sono in offerta questa settimana.
words.exEn: Apples are on special this week.

words.ex: Un chilo di pomodori, per favore.
words.exEn: A kilo of tomatoes, please.

words.ex: Mi dà due etti di prosciutto?
words.exEn: Can I have 200 grams of ham?
words.note: Italians buy deli food by the etto (100 g): mezzo etto = 50 g.

words.ex: Bastano cinquecento grammi di pasta.
words.exEn: Five hundred grams of pasta is enough.

words.ex: Prendo un litro di latte.
words.exEn: I'll get a litre of milk.

words.ex: Compra due pacchi di pasta.
words.exEn: Buy two packets of pasta.

words.ex: Una bottiglia d'acqua, per favore.
words.exEn: A bottle of water, please.

words.ex: Vorrei sei fette di prosciutto.
words.exEn: I'd like six slices of ham.

words.ex: Mi dà un pezzo di parmigiano?
words.exEn: Can I have a piece of Parmesan?

words.ex: Una dozzina di uova, grazie.
words.exEn: A dozen eggs, thanks.

words.ex: Questi pomodori sono molto buoni.
words.exEn: These tomatoes are really good.

words.ex: Prendo un chilo di mele rosse.
words.exEn: I'll take a kilo of red apples.

words.ex: Questo negozio è troppo caro.
words.exEn: This shop is too expensive.
words.note: Also dear: Cara Anna at the start of a letter.

words.ex: Cerco un albergo economico.
words.exEn: I'm looking for a cheap hotel.
words.note: Plural: economici. Also means economic: la crisi economica.

words.ex: Preferisco i capelli corti.
words.exEn: I prefer short hair.
words.note: For height use basso, not corto.

words.ex: La giacca mi sta larga.
words.exEn: The jacket is too big on me.
words.note: False friend: largo = wide/loose, not large (= grande). Plural: larghi.

words.ex: Questi jeans sono stretti.
words.exEn: These jeans are tight.

words.ex: Stasera devo essere elegante.
words.exEn: Tonight I need to look smart.

words.ex: La farmacia è aperta fino alle otto.
words.exEn: The pharmacy is open until eight.

words.ex: Il lunedì mattina molti negozi sono chiusi.
words.exEn: Many shops are closed on Monday mornings.

words.ex: Quanto costano queste scarpe?
words.exEn: How much are these shoes?
words.note: Agrees with the noun: quanti euro? quante mele?

words.ex: Cinquanta euro? È troppo!
words.exEn: Fifty euros? That's too much!

words.ex: Metti il giubbotto, fa freddo.
words.exEn: Put your jacket on, it's cold.

words.ex: Per il colloquio compro una cravatta blu.
words.exEn: I'm buying a blue tie for the interview.

words.ex: Questo piumino è leggero ma caldo.
words.exEn: This down jacket is light but warm.
words.note: Also means a duvet for the bed.

words.ex: Ho un cardigan grigio per l'ufficio.
words.exEn: I have a grey cardigan for the office.

words.ex: Mi serve un paio di calze nere.
words.exEn: I need a pair of black socks.
words.note: Le calze covers socks and tights; short socks are also i calzini.

words.ex: Questi pantaloni hanno quattro tasche.
words.exEn: These trousers have four pockets.

words.ex: Cerco un cappotto beige.
words.exEn: I'm looking for a beige coat.
words.note: Invariable: una borsa beige, due borse beige.

words.ex: La camicia celeste ti sta benissimo.
words.exEn: The light blue shirt really suits you.

words.ex: Ha comprato un vestito lilla.
words.exEn: She bought a lilac dress.
words.note: Invariable, like rosa and viola.

words.ex: Il reso è gratuito entro trenta giorni.
words.exEn: Returns are free within thirty days.

words.ex: Il prezzo è sul cartellino.
words.exEn: The price is on the tag.

words.ex: Quella bancarella vende formaggi buonissimi.
words.exEn: That stall sells really good cheese.

words.ex: Un mazzo di basilico, per favore.
words.exEn: A bunch of basil, please.

words.ex: Il fruttivendolo sotto casa è molto gentile.
words.exEn: The greengrocer near my place is very kind.
words.note: Also the shop itself: vado dal fruttivendolo.

words.ex: Preferisco la maglietta a righe.
words.exEn: I prefer the striped T-shirt.

words.ex: Ha una camicia a quadri rossa.
words.exEn: He has a red checked shirt.

verbs.note: comprare qualcosa a qualcuno = to buy something for someone. Also common: prendere (Lo prendo! = I'll take it).
ex: Ho comprato un regalo per mia madre.
I bought a present for my mother.

verbs.note: vendere qualcosa a qualcuno. In vendita = for sale.
ex: Vendono frutta e verdura al mercato.
They sell fruit and vegetables at the market.
Ho venduto la mia bici vecchia.

verbs.en: to try on; to try; to feel
verbs.note: provare + clothes = to try on. provare a + infinitive = to try to do something.
ex: Can I try on these trousers?

verbs.en: to bring; to carry; to wear
verbs.note: Means both to bring/carry and to wear (glasses, a size): Porto la 42 = I'm a size 42.
Irregular -gli- → -lg- in io and loro: scelgo, scelgono. Participle scelto.
ex: I don't know which one to choose.

verbs.note: Only for money: spendere soldi. For time use passare (passo il weekend al mare). Participle speso.
ex: I spend too much on clothes.

verbs.note: chiedere qualcosa a qualcuno: chiedo il prezzo alla commessa. No preposition before the thing asked for. Participle chiesto.
ex: I'll ask for a bag at the till.

verbs.note: dare qualcosa a qualcuno. In shops: Mi dà un chilo di mele? = Can I have a kilo of apples? Note the accent on dà (gives) vs da (from).
ex: Mi dà due etti di formaggio?
Can I have 200 grams of cheese?

phrases.note: Informal: Posso aiutarti?
phrases.ex: Buongiorno, posso aiutarla? — Sì, cerco una giacca.
phrases.exEn: Good morning, can I help you? — Yes, I'm looking for a jacket.

phrases.ex: Cerca qualcosa? — No, grazie, sto solo dando un'occhiata.
phrases.exEn: Looking for anything? — No thanks, I'm just looking.

phrases.note: Agree the pronoun: provarla (la giacca), provarli (i jeans).
phrases.ex: Mi piace questo maglione. Posso provarlo?
phrases.exEn: I like this sweater. Can I try it on?

phrases.ex: Che taglia porta? — La 44, credo.
phrases.exEn: What size are you? — A 44, I think.

phrases.en: How does it look on me?
phrases.lit: How does it stay on me?
phrases.note: stare bene/male a qualcuno = to suit / not suit someone.
